A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COMPLEXTEMPQA, with the same dataset, taxonomy, and substantial shared experimental content. All 18 pages of v2 and 13 pages of v3, including appendices and visual material, support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original LLM evaluations in Tables 3–7 and a human assessment of 450 questions involving 11 volunteers in Section 5 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V3 retains the original human assessment in Section 5 and Figure 4 and reports original LLM results, including additional GPT evaluations, in Tables 3–7.

M1.justification: The extraction, template generation, multi-hop construction, implicit event naming, and metadata procedures are retained. V3 expands their documentation and renames easy/hard ratings as popular/unpopular. Its comparison of up to three items was already specified in v2 Section 4.3; no procedural revision is established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 100,228,457-question dataset spanning 1987–2023, with attribute, comparison, and counting questions concerning entities, events, and time. The added GPT evaluations retain this coverage; no new dataset, domain, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: V3 adds GPT-4o to the zero-shot comparison and adds both GPT-4o and GPT-3.5 to the few-shot and question-type comparisons in Tables 4, 6, and 7. The RAG comparator set is unchanged. Llama-chat and Llama-2 denote the retained models.

E3.justification: Both versions report zero-shot and 0–3-shot evaluations, the same three DPR context settings, the same tabulated metrics, and the same human-study design. No changed evaluation procedure is specified. The omitted evaluation-sample description and newly disclosed retrieval-corpus settings are documentation changes, not established protocol revisions.

E4.justification: V3 removes the dataset-characterization analyses in v2 Appendices B.1–B.2: page-view distributions with difficulty thresholds and event-category, entity-category, and country distributions in Figures 5–6. This eliminates the supporting analyses of familiarity thresholds and topical/geographic concentration. The human assessment and question-type evaluations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the evaluations. The human-rating chart retains aggregate bars without uncertainty reporting. V3's standard-deviation threshold concerns popularity classification, not uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 3, 4, 6, and 7 add substantial GPT results, with GPT-4o becoming the leading reported F1 model and reaching 45.72 F1 at three shots. GPT-3.5's reported zero-shot F1 changes from 7.74 to 4.56, although identical evaluation samples are not confirmed. V2's appendix popularity and category/country findings are also removed; retained open-model scores and RAG results match.

T1.justification: No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed. The taxonomy remains the same, and v3's worked multi-hop example explains the existing construction rather than introducing new mathematical content.

C1.justification: The principal dataset, taxonomy, complexity, metadata, and benchmarking contributions remain. V3 recasts the advertised rating as popularity and explicitly foregrounds substantial LLM weaknesses on complex temporal questions in its conclusion; v2's conclusion describes the evaluation more generally as providing insights.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive limitations concerning missing source facts, temporal coverage, evolving knowledge, the 2018 retrieval-corpus mismatch, and comparison-question imbalance. It removes v2's detailed explanation of English-Wikipedia-related geographic and event biases and adds stronger GPT-4o generalization interpretations. Some overreach: Section 6.4 claims best recall across categories, although Table 6 gives counting recall of 20.67 for GPT-4o versus 27.44 for Mixtral.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies the December 20, 2018 Wikipedia retrieval corpus, its 21,015,324 passages, title/[SEP] preprocessing, and popularity-threshold and timestamp-filtering details. It removes v2's disclosure of 12,000 evaluation questions sampled equally across types and substantially shortens Appendix A's template catalog. Experiment prompts, metadata fields, and dataset/code access remain.

R1.justification: V3 removes SQuAD 2.0 and CNN/Daily Mail from the related-dataset table and prunes discussion and citations concerning knowledge-graph question generation, event-focused retrieval, and collective memory. It adds the FlashAttention citation in the model descriptions. The central positioning around temporal-QA scale and complexity remains.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction, dataset description, construction explanation, experimental discussion, and conclusion. It reorganizes experiments into numbered subsections, groups and condenses question templates, moves Dataset Use to Appendix E and model descriptions to Appendix C, and introduces a dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column layout with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. V2's detailed appendix pipeline figure is replaced by a simplified main-text Figure 3; Table 8 and Figures 5–6 disappear. Comparison tables gain GPT rows, and the retained quality chart changes its difficulty labels to popularity labels.

improvement.justification: V3 improves explanations, specifies the retrieval corpus, expands GPT comparisons, and explicitly discusses important limitations. However, it removes the evaluation-sample specification and dataset-bias analyses and introduces claims of GPT-4o dominance that its own tables contradict. These gains in clarity and coverage coexist with losses in reproducibility and interpretive accuracy, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
